item.title: OrangeDB: Distributed NoSQL Key-Document Database
item.description:
GitHub (Orange) · GitHub (Parrot) · GitHub (Orangectl) · Architecture Post

OrangeDB is a lightweight, distributed, cloud-native NoSQL key-document database written in Go. It blends architectural concepts from systems like Cassandra, MongoDB, RocksDB, LevelDB, and CockroachDB to achieve high write throughput, predictable low-latency reads, and horizontal scalability across Kubernetes clusters.

The Orange Ecosystem 

flowchart TD
Client["Application Client"] --> Gate["Orangegate (Proxy & Query Router)"]
subgraph K8s["Kubernetes Cluster (Managed by Orangectl)"]
Gate --> S1["Shard 1 Leader"]
Gate --> S2["Shard 2 Leader"]
Gate --> S3["Shard 3 Leader"]
subgraph Shard1["Shard 1 Cluster"]
S1 <-->|"Replication"| R1["Replica 1"]
S1 <-->|"Replication"| R2["Replica 2"]
end
subgraph NodeInternal["OrangeDB Node Engine"]
OQL["OQL Query Parser & Validator"] --> Parrot["Parrot LSM Storage Engine"]
Parrot --> MemQueue["Chain of Memtables"]
Parrot --> WAL["Write-Ahead Log"]
Parrot --> SST["SSTables (mmap & Bloom Filters)"]
end
end

Components

  1. OrangeDB Core: The database server handling primary-key indexing, native binary document serialization, schema validation, and SQL-like querying via OQL (Orange Query Language).
  2. Parrot Storage Engine: An embedded Log-Structured Merge (LSM) tree engine built for maximum I/O concurrency and write performance.
  3. Orangegate: A high-performance stateless proxy placed in front of the cluster to route read/write queries to the correct partition owners and perform quorum aggregation.
  4. Orangectl: A custom Kubernetes Operator providing CRDs to automate cluster provisioning, autoscaling, master failover, and data rebalancing.

Parrot LSM Storage Engine Innovations

Traditional B-Trees suffer from write amplification because updating records incurs random disk writes across multiple tree levels. LSM trees write sequentially to an append-only log, dramatically accelerating write operations.

Parrot introduces key architectural enhancements over conventional LSM engines:

1. Chain of Memtables (Uninterrupted Writes)

Standard double-buffered LSM trees pause incoming writes when both active and flushing memtables become full. Parrot employs a queue/chain of memtables:

  • Ingestion continuously appends new immutable memtables to the queue.
  • Background flush workers consume independently from the tail, eliminating write stalls under bursty workloads.

2. Zero-Copy mmap Reads

Parrot reads on-disk SSTable blocks via shared memory mapping (mmap). Operating system page caches are accessed directly without copying block payloads into user-space buffers, minimizing CPU cache misses and memory churn.

3. Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC)

Minimizes lock contention across concurrent read/write transactions by leveraging lock-free atomic pointers for memtable switching and versioned SSTable manifest tracking.

Feature Matrix

  • Document Model: JSON-like schema-free or strict schema-validated document storage.
  • Native Binary Encoding: Efficient serialization reducing network payloads and disk space.
  • Crash Recovery: Append-only Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) ensures ACID durability.
  • Compaction: Multi-level background compaction removes stale tombstones and deduplicates updated records.
  • High Availability: Configurable Quorum reads (R+W>NR + W > NR+W>N) and synchronous/asynchronous replica synchronization.
  • Kubernetes Native: Automated deployment and lifecycle management via CRDs and Helm charts.

Quickstart & Installation

Standalone Installation 

# Install Orange CLI / server
go install github.com/nagarajpoojari404/orange@latest

# Start OrangeDB standalone server
orange start --port 8080 --data-dir ./orange-data

Cluster Deployment via Kubernetes (orangectl) 

# Install Orangectl Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs)
kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nagarajpoojari404/orangectl/main/dist/install.yaml

# Deploy an OrangeDB 3-node sharded cluster
kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nagarajpoojari404/orangectl/main/config/samples/cluster_v1_orange.yaml

Load Testing with k6 

k6 run k6/stress_test.js
k6 run k6/load_test.js

item.title: Ripple MQ: High-Performance Distributed Event Streaming
item.description:
GitHub (Server) · GitHub (Go Client) · GitHub (Benchmark)

Ripple MQ is a high-throughput, ultra-low latency distributed in-memory event streaming engine written in Go. Designed for large-scale telemetry ingestion, real-time message broadcasting, and event-driven microservice architectures, Ripple combines a single-threaded non-blocking I/O event loop with lock-free memory buffers to achieve high message rates while keeping CPU overhead minimal.

Architecture & Design 

flowchart LR
Producer["Event Producers / Apps"] -->|"Custom TCP Protocol"| EventLoop["Non-Blocking I/O Event Loop"]
subgraph RippleCore["Ripple Server Engine"]
EventLoop --> Demux["Message Demultiplexer"]
Demux --> TopicA["Topic A Partition 0"]
Demux --> TopicB["Topic A Partition 1"]
Demux --> TopicC["Topic B Partition 0"]
TopicA --> MemRing["In-Memory Ring Buffers"]
TopicB --> MemRing
TopicC --> MemRing
end
MemRing --> PushStream["Zero-Copy Push Dispatcher"]
PushStream --> Consumer1["Consumer Group Alpha"]
PushStream --> Consumer2["Consumer Group Beta"]

Core Innovations

  • Single-Threaded Non-Blocking I/O: Eliminates thread context-switching overhead and multi-threaded mutex lock contention on the hot path by processing network frames sequentially on an optimized event loop.
  • In-Memory Ring Buffers: Employs circular memory structures with zero-copy slice slicing for message ingestion and fan-out consumption.
  • Custom Wire Protocol: Lightweight binary framing over raw TCP avoids the heavy serialization overhead and HTTP/2 framing tax associated with gRPC and REST.
  • Partitioned Topic Queues: Supports horizontal stream partitioning to allow parallel consumption across independent consumer worker pools.

Ecosystem Components

  1. ripple-server: The core messaging engine handling client connections, partition management, and message dispatch.
  2. go-client: An ergonomic, production-grade Go SDK for producing and consuming message streams with automatic connection pooling and reconnect handling.
  3. benchmark: A high-concurrency performance benchmarking and stress-testing tool evaluating throughput, p99 latency, and saturation points against Apache Kafka and RabbitMQ.

Client SDK Usage (Go) 

package main

import (
 "context"
 "fmt"
 "log"

 "github.com/ripple-mq/go-client"
)

func main() {
 // Initialize Ripple client connection
 client, err := ripple.NewClient(ripple.Config{
 Addr: "127.0.0.1:9092",
 })
 if err != nil {
 log.Fatalf("Failed to connect to Ripple MQ: %v", err)
 }
 defer client.Close()

 // Publish an event to topic 'orders'
 err = client.Publish(context.Background(), "orders", []byte(`{"order_id": "1001", "amount": 49.99}`))
 if err != nil {
 log.Fatalf("Publish failed: %v", err)
 }
 fmt.Println("Event published successfully!")

 // Subscribe and consume events
 sub, err := client.Subscribe(context.Background(), "orders", "analytics-consumer-group")
 if err != nil {
 log.Fatalf("Subscription failed: %v", err)
 }

 for msg := range sub.Messages() {
 fmt.Printf("Received message: %s\n", string(msg.Payload))
 msg.Ack()
 }
}

Benchmarking & Local Setup 

# Clone the server repository
git clone https://github.com/ripple-mq/ripple-server.git
cd ripple-server

# Install dependencies and build
make install
make build

# Start Ripple server
./bin/ripple-server --config config.yaml

# Run benchmarks
git clone https://github.com/ripple-mq/benchmark.git
cd benchmark && go run main.go --target 127.0.0.1:9092 --concurrency 50 --messages 1000000

item.title: PandaFS (nanoDFS): Distributed Fault-Tolerant File System
item.description:
GitHub Organization (nanoDFS) · Master Node · Slave (Chunk Server) · Go Client SDK · P2P Library

PandaFS (developed under the nanoDFS organization) is a fault-tolerant, scalable, distributed file system modeled after the Google File System (GFS) architecture. Written in Go, it is engineered for high-bandwidth streaming reads and writes over large datasets across clusters of commodity hardware.

Architectural Topology 

flowchart TD
Client["nanoDFS Client SDK"] <-->|"1. Metadata / Chunk Locations"| Master["nanoDFS Master Node"]
subgraph StorageCluster["Distributed Chunk Servers"]
Client <-->|"2. Encrypted Chunk Stream"| Chunk1["Slave Node 1 (Primary)"]
Chunk1 <-->|"3. P2P Replication Pipeline"| Chunk2["Slave Node 2 (Secondary)"]
Chunk2 <-->|"4. P2P Replication Pipeline"| Chunk3["Slave Node 3 (Tertiary)"]
end
Master <-->|"Heartbeats & Reports"| Chunk1
Master <-->|"Heartbeats & Reports"| Chunk2
Master <-->|"Heartbeats & Reports"| Chunk3

Core Architecture Components

  1. Master Node (nanoDFS/Master):

    • Manages the entire filesystem namespace, access control lists (ACL), and file-to-chunk mappings.
    • Monitors chunk server health through periodic heartbeats and initiates automated re-replication upon node failure.
    • Never sits in the direct data transfer path, preventing bottlenecking on high-volume reads and writes.

  2. Slave / Chunk Servers (nanoDFS/Slave):

    • Stores 64MB fixed-size file chunks directly on local storage.
    • Computes checksums per chunk to identify silent bit rot and data corruption.
    • Executes peer-to-peer chunk replication pipelines across secondary replicas.

  3. P2P Transport Protocol (nanoDFS/p2p):

    • Custom low-level networking library maintaining persistent, bidirectional TCP connections between peer storage nodes.

  4. Security & Cryptography:

    • Client-Side Encryption: Files are encrypted with symmetric keys (e.g. AES-256) on the client before being streamed to chunk servers.
    • Token-Based Access Control: Master issues time-bound cryptographic tokens for authorized chunk reads and writes.

Client SDK Quickstart (Go)

Install the SDK:

go get github.com/nanoDFS/client-sdk

Upload and download files securely:

package main

import (
 "fmt"
 "log"

 "github.com/nanoDFS/client-sdk/crypto"
 "github.com/nanoDFS/client-sdk/fs"
)

func main() {
 // Generate or load client encryption key
 cryptoKey := crypto.DefaultCryptoKey()
 client := fs.NewFileSystem()

 // Upload a file to PandaFS (automatically chunked, encrypted, and replicated)
 fileID, userID, err := client.Upload(cryptoKey, "./dataset.tar.gz")
 if err != nil {
 log.Fatalf("Failed to upload file: %v", err)
 }
 fmt.Printf("Uploaded successfully! FileID: %s, UserID: %s\n", fileID, userID)

 // Download and decrypt the file
 err = client.Download(fileID, userID, cryptoKey, "./downloads/dataset_restored.tar.gz")
 if err != nil {
 log.Fatalf("Failed to download file: %v", err)
 }
 fmt.Println("File downloaded and verified successfully!")
}

Key Capabilities

  • Automatic Fault Recovery: Degraded chunks are automatically detected and restored to maintain replication invariants.
  • Append-Focused Streaming: Optimized for large sequential writes and concurrent reader streams.
  • Zero Metadata Contention: Chunk servers independently manage physical I/O without querying the Master on each read operation.
